newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf oil product outlook - suffering with crude.
newsitem.headline: Gulf oil product outlook - suffering with crude.

text.p: Gulf oil product prices have little choice in the coming week other than to track volatile crude markets and a trader's gas oil marketing strategy in Singapore, Gulf oil traders said on Thursday.
Gulf premiums to price quotes are expected to come under pressure amid a seasonal downturn and a lack of serious Indian diesel buying till the end of next month, they said.
"It looks bad for the middle of the barrel," said one foreign oil executive based in the Gulf.

Despite heavy recent gas oil buying by a trader in the Singapore market and sales of Mideast gas oil to the region, middle distillate premiums were seen ebbing further on good trader availability and limited Indian subcontinent demand.
The lack of any major refinery maintainance work underway in the Gulf also ensured that the market remained well supplied in the short term, traders said.
Gas oil's premium was assessed at around 25-40 cents to independent fob Gulf price quotes -- 15-20 cents down on the week -- with kerosene's premium 5-10 cents below this.
Naphtha premiums also appeared to be giving up some of its recent Asian petrochemical demand, softening $1-2 a tonne to around $14, traders said.
Gulf product prices fell following steep falls in crude markets on Wednesday when supply length and high inventories took U.S. crude futures to their lowest level since March 1996.
Gas oil was unchanged over the week at $25.30 a barrel fob Gulf while kerosene was steady at $24.10.
Losses in Singapore naphtha markets and crude pushed Gulf naphtha to $195 a tonne from $200.
Outstanding Asian tender requirements, led by Sri Lanka and Nepal, were unlikely on their own to fan premiums higher or shape outright prices, traders said.
